checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Both instruments visible are tall, extending from the lap/legs of the seated/standing players up well above their heads, consistent with the ~1.3m height of a bassoon.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The instrument on the right clearly shows the long boot joint at the bottom curving back up to the wing joint, creating the characteristic U-profile. The bell is at the top.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The internal bore structure is not visible from the exterior; only the external tube doubling back is observable.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: On the right-hand instrument, a thin curved metal tube (bocal) is visible emerging from the top of the wing joint, leading towards where the reed would be.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Numerous metal keys and tone holes distributed along length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Silver-colored keywork mechanisms are clearly visible along the length of both wooden bodies, particularly on the lower joints and the wing joint.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Bell flares outward at top and instrument held diagonally across body when played.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bells at the top of both instruments show the characteristic flare. They are held diagonally across the players' torsos, supported by seat straps (visible on the right player).

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The keys appear silver/nickel-plated, contrasting with the dark wood.
The main body segments are clearly made of turned wood.
